# Introduction

This report demonstrates a polyglot Quarto pipeline using T-Lang as the orchestrator. We combine R, Python, and Julia computations within a single Quarto document, all while using LaTeX for mathematical notation.

```{t}
#| include: false
# Define polyglot helpers that handle path interpolation
r = \(code) {
  final_code = str_replace(code, "$df_r_path", df_r_path)
  write_text("temp.R", final_code)
  run("Rscript temp.R")
}
py = \(code) {
  final_code = str_replace(code, "$df_py_path", df_py_path)
  write_text("temp.py", final_code)
  run("python temp.py")
}
jl = \(code) {
  final_code = str_replace(code, "$df_jl_path", df_jl_path)
  write_text("temp.jl", final_code)
  run("julia temp.jl")
}
```

## R Node Output

The R node generated the following data:

```{t}
#| label: r-data
#| echo: true
df_r_path = read_node("r_data")
r(<{
  df <- read.csv("$df_r_path")
  print(head(df))
}>)
```

## Python Node Output

The Python node generated the following data:

```{t}
#| label: py-data
#| echo: true
df_py_path = read_node("py_data")
py(<{
  import pandas as pd
  df = pd.read_csv("$df_py_path")
  print(df.head())
}>)
```

## Julia Node Output

The Julia node generated the following data:

```{t}
df_jl_path = read_node("jl_data")
jl(<{
  using DataFrames, CSV
  df = CSV.read("$df_jl_path", DataFrame)
  println(first(df, 5))
}>)
```

## Mathematical Modeling (LaTeX)

The relationship being explored across these languages can be represented as:

$$
\mathcal{L} = \sum_{i=1}^{n} (y_i - f(x_i; \theta))^2 + \lambda \|\theta\|_2^2
$$

## Conclusion

T-Lang successfully coordinated data generation in R, Python, and Julia, passed those artifacts to this Quarto document, and used LaTeX to produce this professional report.
